conviction_note: Evidence offsets. Against the print: the H2 ramp the company's own guide needs (H1 FCF -$154M against a ~$250M FY guide; the $105M AOI raise in July was exactly the one-off tariff benefit, so the underlying $450-500M guide needs ~$280-330M in H2 against ~$170M underlying in H1) and the Citi Sell on FCF. For it: a 28%-of-shares, 15-days-to-cover short that squeezed the last two prints by +43% and +32%, a 27% fall since 11 Sep, Canon's 27 Oct read that US print 'remained solid' with its Printing outlook raised, and a 7.3% holder publicly expecting an XFS/deleveraging update on the day. Findings sum to -0.2 and p_up is 50, so the scaled number is 0. abs_move is set at the 20.45% option-implied move, which is well above the 12.45% historical median, because the short is crowded and the last two reactions were 32-43%.
bar: Thin and partly unsourced. Q3 EPS consensus is one analyst at -$0.06 (MarketBeat https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/XRX/earnings/); a preview snippet quoted -$0.12 EPS and $1.86B revenue (gurufocus, returned 403, snippet only). The company guide is the reliable bar: FY2026 revenue ~$7.6B, adjusted operating income $555-605M (includes a $105M one-off tariff benefit), FCF ~$250M (includes $80M tariff-receivable proceeds expected to be reclassified into operating cash flow) (Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001770450/000177045026000034/ex991xrx630268-ker.htm). H1 revenue was $3,768M, so H2 needs ~$3.83B. Findings on the reported-quarter beat or miss are capped small because the street bar is single-source.
positioning_check: Short interest 37,174,860 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, ~28.3% of 131.3M shares outstanding, 14.93 days to cover. It was 40.5M at 08-31 and 39.0M at 09-30, so shorts trimmed slightly into the print (https://equibles.com/stocks/xrx/short-interest). The skew is +33.4 vol points 25d put over call, so downside is paid; the ATM spread is 46% of mid, so the implied move is indicative only. Run-up is -8.2% over 5 days and -20.7% over 20 days; spot is $2.515 against $3.43 on 2026-09-11 (Form 4 tax-withholding price). The last two prints, both against this short base, moved +43.3% and +32.2%.

findings.finding: Peer read-through from Canon's Q3 2026 results deck, a primary document dated 2026-10-27, two days before XRX reports. Canon says the U.S. 'remained solid' while Europe stayed weak. It raised its FY Printing outlook (net sales +¥35.2bn to ¥2,579bn) 'reflecting improved 3Q performance'. Office MFD local-currency sales were -0.4%, hardware -5% and non-hardware +1%, with MFD units -5%. Q4 memory procurement prices were 'finalized in line with expectations'. Against that, memory cost Canon ¥19.8bn of Q3 operating profit, and Printing operating profit fell 3% y/y. Net, the read is a stable US office market with heavy component cost; Xerox's Q2 pro forma decline was -6.5%, worse than this peer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: XRX has moved hard on pro forma revenue: Q3 2025 missed on revenue (-7.8% pro forma) and fell 9.9%; Q2 2026 beat revenue ($1.92B vs $1.90B) with a raised guide and rose 32.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Released 27 Oct, and XRX kept falling into the print (5-day run-up -8.2%). If the market had taken a 'US solid, printing raised' read-through, XRX would not be at its low of the month with puts bid at +33 vol points. Canon is a Japanese filer that XRX's one-analyst coverage does not cite.
findings.independence: Proxy, not Xerox's own number. HP's FQ3 (to July, reported 2026-08-26) points the other way and is older: print -2% (-4% cc), commercial print units -2% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000047217/000004721726000048/hp73126exhibit991q326.htm). Filed separately below.

findings.finding: HP Inc FQ3 2026 (quarter to July, released 2026-08-26). Printing revenue was $3.9B, -2% y/y (-4% constant currency); commercial printing revenue -1%; commercial hardware units -2%; supplies -3%; management flagged rising component costs. That is a soft but not collapsing print market overlapping Xerox's Q3, consistent with continued mid-single-digit pro forma declines at Xerox.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As above: pro forma revenue misses cost XRX 9.9% in Oct 2025; beats bought +32% in Jul 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is two months old and XRX traded up to $3.43 after it. Filed for breadth, sized small.
findings.independence: Cuts against the Canon finding in direction; different company and different quarter end. none other.

findings.finding: FCF guide arithmetic: Q1 2026 FCF was -$165M and Q2 +$11M, so H1 = -$154M. The FY guide is ~$250M and 'reflects proceeds from the sale of IEEPA tariff receivables' ($80M, expected to be reclassified into operating cash flow). H2 therefore needs roughly $325M of FCF beyond the reclassification, or about $400M if it is not reclassified. The year-ago Q3 delivered $131M. A Q3 FCF short of ~$130-160M, or a trimmed FY FCF guide, lands on the line a $4.2B-debt, Caa2-rated company trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Oct 2025 a revenue miss and a cut FY revenue view sent the stock -9.9%, and July 2025's guidance cut sent it -22.4%. Q1 2026 reaffirmed the FCF guide with Q1 FCF at -$165M and the stock rose 43.3%, so a reaffirmation on a low bar has paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Citi's 8 Oct Sell cited FCF, and the stock is -20.7% over 20 days with puts bid. What is not visible is the size of the H2 hurdle relative to the year-ago Q3 ($131M). The one-analyst coverage (one EPS estimate) has published no FCF number. If the market fully priced a cut, the 28% short would be covering rather than holding near its highs.
findings.independence: Citi's 8 Oct downgrade on FCF generation concerns (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/why-xerox-xrx-shares-getting-233910870.html). Shares the Q2 release with the AOI finding below; the FCF hurdle partly derives from the same H2 profit ramp.

findings.finding: The July AOI guide raise was entirely the one-off. Adjusted operating income guidance went from $450-500M to $555-605M, a $105M raise that equals the $105M IEEPA tariff-receivable benefit booked in Q2 Print and Other profit; the release says the guide 'reflects' it. Underlying, the FY guide is unchanged at $450-500M. H1 underlying AOI is ~$170M (Q1 $72M plus Q2 $203M less $105M), so H2 needs ~$280-330M, i.e. $140-165M a quarter. Q2 underlying was ~$98M and Q3 2025 AOI margin was 3.3%. Delivery rests on the Lexmark synergy target (raised to at least $350M) against memory and oil cost headwinds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2025 (guide cut) -22.4%; Q2 2026 (headline guide raise) +32.2%, then the stock gave back ~15% over the following weeks per Zacks (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2966735/xerox-stock-falls-155-since-q2-earnings-revenue-beat).
findings.why_not_priced: Wire summaries reported the raise as 'raises FY AOI guidance' (https://www.enxmag.com/twii/news/2026/07/xeroxs-strong-q2-raises-full%e2%80%91year-2026-guidance/), and the single EPS estimate (-$0.06) leaves the underlying ramp unmodelled. Partly priced through the post-Q2 give-back. Shrunk for the crowded short.
findings.independence: Same document as the FCF finding; counts as related, not independent. Year-ago Q3 margin from the Q3 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1770450/000177045025000033/ex991xrx930258-ker.htm).

findings.finding: Crowded short into a fallen stock: 37.2M shares short (28.3% of shares outstanding, 14.9 days to cover) at 2026-10-15. Spot $2.515 is 27% below the $3.43 of 2026-09-11. The last two prints against the same short base moved +43.3% and +32.2%, both cases where the bar was low and the company reaffirmed or raised guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 +43.3% and Q2 2026 +32.2%, each on ~10-20x normal volume (baseline). The four prints before that, with a smaller short, were all negative.
findings.why_not_priced: The put skew (+33 vol points) and the 20-day drawdown say the option market leans down. A squeeze is a mechanism that only fires if the release clears the low bar, and at 15 days to cover the short cannot exit before the print.
findings.independence: Baseline reaction history (+43.3%, +32.2%) and the Form 4 price of $3.43 on 2026-09-11 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1770450/000119312526391896/xslF345X06/ownership.xml).

findings.finding: Activist catalyst on the day. STARTEEPO and Frantisek Bostl hold 7.34% (8.0M shares via the fund plus 1.5M shares and 140k calls direct; 13D/A filed 2026-09-08) and have asked for a formal strategic review and separate disclosure of Xerox Financial Services, which they value at $7.69 a share. Their 2026-10-19 letter says conversations with Xerox have been 'encouraging' and that they expect Xerox to use the 29 Oct release to update shareholders on XFS transparency, the review and deleveraging. Any XFS disclosure, review or monetization announced with the print would be new.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior XRX print has carried an asset-monetization announcement. The Feb 2026 $450M TPG IP JV was a balance-sheet action and was not a print-day item.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell ~8% the week after the letter (to $2.56 on 23 Oct per stockanalysis) and sits at a 27% discount to September, so the market assigns little probability to an update. If it believed one, the 28% short would be covering ahead of it.
findings.independence: 13D/A primary document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1770450/000149315226041719/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml). Nothing from Xerox itself confirms any review.

findings.finding: Citi downgraded XRX to Sell from Neutral on 2026-10-08 (PT $2.50 from $3.45; the stock now trades at the target). It cited FCF generation, a 'structurally challenged' print market, possible demand pull-forward in IT Solutions and integration friction from a sales-force reorganization. IT Solutions revenue was already -8.9% in Q2 at a 3.7% margin, and Q2 pro forma equipment sales were -13%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: IT Solutions -8.9% and equipment -13% pro forma were looked through, and the stock rose 32.2% on the headline AOI.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: wire coverage, and the stock has fallen to the $2.50 target. Filed because the pull-forward and reorganization claims are specific Q3 operating risks that could appear in equipment and IT Solutions revenue.
findings.independence: Shares the FCF concern with the FCF finding. IT Solutions and equipment numbers come from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001770450/000177045026000034/ex991xrx630268-ker.htm).

outside_window.finding: The 2028 maturity wall and refinancing (Moody's Caa2, negative outlook, March 2026). The 8.875% 2029 notes become callable at fixed prices after 2026-11-30. Any refinancing announcement is undated and not expected inside the window.

baseline_tension: The negatives (the FCF and AOI ramp, Citi) agree with the +33 vol-point put skew and the -20.7% 20-day run-up, so they are probably largely priced. The positives (crowded short with two consecutive 30%+ squeezes, Canon's US read, the activist's expected update) cut against the skew. Balanced, so p_up stays at 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short against a negative, and negatives agreeing with a strong skew): applied once per negative. FCF guide -2.5 to -2.0, AOI underlying ramp -1.5 to -1.0, Citi -1.0 to -0.6.

Positioning finding +3.0 to +2.0: the crowded-short effect is already carried by shrinking the negatives, and lesson 5 says positioning alone is not a cause. Trimmed to avoid counting the squeeze twice. The drawdown has a named cause (Citi), so it is not an 'unexplained drawdown' finding.
Starteepo finding +1.5 to +1.2: nothing from Xerox confirms a review; lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number).
Lesson 6 (bar single-source): reported-quarter findings (Canon +0.5, HP -0.3, Citi) kept small. The guidance findings are measured against the company's own FY guide, which is sourced.
Lessons 2/5 left the Canon and HP proxies standing at small sizes and confirmed the AOI finding as a guidance item, not a one-off.
